key_insight: In a 100.7 GW North Sea offshore wind scenario, engineering wake models can match annual capacity factors while still showing sizable month-by-month and regime-dependent wind-speed biases relative to LES and mesoscale simulations.
engineering_relevance: Regional wind-energy planning should account for wake-model choice because formulation-dependent errors of 0.60-0.70 m/s at 10-40 km downstream can materially affect offshore energy and layout assessments.
method: Compared HARMONIE-AROME mesoscale simulations, ASPIRE LES, and three engineering wake models (Jensen, Bastankhah Gaussian, TurbOPark).
Evaluated year-round offshore wind conditions across wind speed and atmospheric stability regimes.
Benchmarked model free-stream and wake predictions for a large 2050 North Sea offshore wind buildout.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that LES and mesoscale simulations reproduce observed local free-stream winds well, while all three engineering wake models overpredict mean wind speed versus LES in every month, with the largest biases at 10-40 km downstream.
watch_item: Good annual energy agreement can hide systematic spatial and seasonal wake errors, so relying on a single wake formulation may understate uncertainty in cluster-scale offshore planning.
paper_title: Wake effects in a 100 GW North Sea offshore wind scenario: a model intercomparison under year-round weather conditions
